assumptions.what: Network training: tanh hidden units, logistic (or softmax) output, cross-entropy with weight decay 0.01, L-BFGS for at most 200 iterations, weights uniform in ±1/sqrt(fan-in), seeded. The paper gives only the architecture (one hidden layer of 10 units).

assumptions.what: Jaeger's 'masked out clustering': k-means (k = 50, correlation distance) on the 500 genes with the largest Welch t, then genes taken in order of t, each masking the rest of its cluster. The paper gives only '50 clusters, then the top 30 genes by t-test'.
assumptions.sensitivity: hyp.prefilter2000 (2,000 genes clustered) on the same three runs.

assumptions.what: Each feature scaled to z-scores on the bootstrap resample; PCA on centred, unscaled genes; the data used as found in the Kent Ridge 'transformed' files, as the paper says (the prostate test arrays average about 12 times the training arrays' intensity).
assumptions.sensitivity: hyp.scaled (each array scaled to the same mean intensity) on the prostate test set.

assumptions.what: Feature selection redone on every bootstrap resample (the paper: 'after obtaining the transformed resampling data, we extract and select features').
assumptions.sensitivity: hyp.once (features chosen once on all training samples) on the same three runs.

assumptions.what: Seeds: our run is seed 0 (each fold seeded by its index); the paper gives none.
assumptions.sensitivity: Test sets rerun with seeds 0 to 4 (tables.json, seeds).

cause.summary: Lung comes back (149 of 149). Prostate: 31 of 34 against 33; scaling each array to the same mean intensity, a step the paper does not mention, gives exactly 33 of 34 on all five seeds, so the gap is how the test experiment, about 12 times brighter than the training arrays, was handled. ALL-AML: 33 of 34 against 34; the same test sample (31st in the file) is wrong in every seed and every variant we tried.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The prostate test arrays (a different experiment, about 12 times the training arrays' mean intensity) need per-array scaling

weight decay 1e-3 and 1e-1, 50 and 1000 L-BFGS iterations (hyp.alpha*, hyp.iter*): 33, 29, 33, 33 of 34

hypotheses.test: hyp.once, hyp.hard, hyp.prefilter2000: 33 of 34 each
